Full-time ICT Business Analyst position available with competitive salary. Work in a dynamic team in Altona North, VIC 3025. Apply today through 11 Recruitment!

3 Stand-out Bullet Points:
•	Full-Time ICT Business Analyst
•	$80,000 p.a. plus superannuation 
•	Work in a professional environment.

Position Overview:
HYDAC Pty Ltd - HYDAC is a global provider of hydraulics, filtration and fluid technology solutions serving industrial sectors worldwide.
As an ICT Business Analyst at HYDAC Pty Ltd, you will be responsible for analysing business requirements and improving the digital systems that support engineering, sales, inventory, service and operational workflows. This position requires strong analytical thinking, stakeholder engagement and the ability to translate operational needs into practical ICT solutions.

Responsibilities and Tasks:

•	Work with users across engineering, sales, supply chain, service, finance and administration to formulate and document business and ICT requirements.
•	Identify, investigate and analyse business processes, procedures and work practices supporting HYDAC's hydraulic, filtration and fluid technology operations.
•	Identify system inefficiencies, deficiencies and limitations, and recommend improved business practices, system functionality and workflow behaviour.
•	Apply project management methodologies, principles and techniques to develop plans and assist with the costing, resourcing and delivery of ICT improvement projects.
•	Develop functional specifications for system developers, technology vendors and integration partners.
•	Use data and process modelling techniques to prepare clear system specifications for enterprise applications, reporting tools and system integrations.
•	Take responsibility for deploying functional solutions, including preparing and implementing system test plans to ensure acceptable quality, integrity and performance.
•	Create user guides, process documentation and training materials, and deliver training to employees using new or updated systems.
•	Act as a central reference point for ICT projects, providing guidance and information to support system proposals, priorities and decision-making.
•	Facilitate stakeholder workshops and interviews, maintain requirements traceability, and manage changes to agreed business and system requirements.
•	Coordinate system upgrades, integrations and releases with internal teams and external providers, supporting user acceptance testing, rollout and issue resolution.
•	Monitor post-implementation outcomes, analyse system performance and user feedback, and recommend continuous improvements to digital workflows and reporting.

Qualifications and Skills:

•	Relevant qualification.
•	Minimum 1 year experience as an ICT Business Analyst
•	Strong business process analysis, requirements gathering and documentation skills
•	Experience with process mapping, data modelling and functional specification development
•	Ability to analyse and improve enterprise systems, integrations and reporting workflows
•	Strong stakeholder communication, workshop facilitation, problem-solving and project coordination skills

Salary: The role offers a remuneration package of $80,000 p.a plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

How to Apply: 11 Recruitment is your pathway to securing this exciting opportunity. We are looking forward to facilitating your application and potentially welcoming you to a company that values expertise. Apply now and let us help you take the next step in your career.

result.description:
At Qantas, our teams come together to create new and unique experiences for our customers.
A fantastic opportunity to be part of a team that focuses on cutting-edge technology and quality engineering principles.
Full-time and permanent position based at our new Product Innovation Centre in Adelaide. 


Join Qantas in our brand-new Product Innovation Centre located in Adelaide to help us ensure consumer needs are met by embedding robust testing strategies and automation practices that uphold software reliability, performance, and security. Deliver seamless, high-quality digital experiences that build customer trust and satisfaction.



As a Senior Quality Engineer – Conversational AI, you’ll be responsible for testing and validating chatbot solutions while helping shape and evolve our CAI quality engineering capability. You’ll work closely with product, engineering and AI teams to design automated chatbot tests, validate conversation flows, and troubleshoot issues as they arise. With the freedom to identify and implement the best solutions, you’ll continuously improve our tools, frameworks and overall approach to CAI testing.



You’ll Have

Strong experience in Quality Engineering or QA, with hands-on experience testing Conversational AI or chatbot platforms
Proven experience using Cyara Botium for chatbot test automation
Expertise in testing conversation flows, intents, entities and dialogue management across multiple scenarios
Experience validating chatbot integrations with backend systems and APIs
Ability to design and execute end-to-end test strategies for AI-driven customer experiences
Experience embedding chatbot testing into CI/CD pipelines
Strong understanding of the challenges of testing AI systems, including ambiguity, edge cases and training data validation
Experience testing non-functional requirements such as performance, security and accessibility in conversational interfaces
Confidence collaborating with cross-functional teams to embed quality early in the delivery lifecycle
Strong analytical skills to interpret chatbot behaviour and translate insights into quality improvements
Excellent communication, documentation and stakeholder engagement skills
Experience working with Mobile apps as the entry point to the chat bot.
A continuous improvement mindset and passion for emerging AI technologies
Confidence contributing to go/no-go decisions for chatbot and CAI releases


Why Qantas?

At Qantas, your career can take you further than you imagined. You’ll join a team where creativity and passion drives success. Together we dream big and deliver even bigger. 

You’ll find diverse opportunities to grow, personally and professionally. From day one, you’ll be supported with hands-on training, coaching, and formal learning programs designed to help you excel. Your development is our priority because we know that when you thrive, so do our customers. 

And while this role is your starting point at Qantas, it’s just the beginning. We have a proud history of helping our people explore new paths and reach new heights - the destinations are endless. 


The Qantas employee benefits program offers amazing benefits that extend well beyond travel.  

We love to travel: Enjoy heavily discounted air travel within Australia and across the globe, both for you and your family and friends, as well as exclusive deals on accommodation and holidays.
We have flexible leave options: Make use of leave and flexible working opportunities including 18 weeks paid parental leave and the option to purchase additional paid leave for eligible employees.
We’ll give you access to thousands of rewards: Through our partnerships we can offer you discounts across shopping, food and wine, insurance, health and wellbeing, leisure and entertainment. You can also take advantage of our salary packaging program including motor vehicles, eligible portable electronic devices and professional memberships.
We’ll support your wellbeing: Whether it’s learning to better support your own and others’ mental health, our interactive wellbeing app or your very own tailored nutrition plan. 

Apply at the earliest to be considered!

Qantas is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing a working environment that embraces and values diversity and inclusion. By coming to work for us, you’ll be part of an organisation that encourages diversity, supports charities and environmental initiatives. We encourage Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, and people of all backgrounds to apply. If you have any support or access requirements, we encourage you to advise us at time of application. Your personal information will be kept confidential in compliance with relevant privacy legislation.

Software Engineer
About the company:
At Directwire our team knows all Full Stack Java based technologies  and best practices better than anyone else. You’ll have access to seasoned professionals in ANZAC region who can advise you across Java based platforms and provide a level of support and knowledge that gives you and your team greater efficiency, confidence, and peace of mind along the implementation, upgrade, or migration journey.
 About the role:
We are currently seeking an experienced Very Senior Software Engineer - Full Stack Java Technologies (15+ years' experience) to join our friendly and supportive team in Parramatta on a permanent full-time basis.
Location: Parramatta, NSW
Salary range: $150,000 - $180,000
Role: Full-time
Positions: Multiple
Key responsibilities include: 
•	Analyse client business processes, user requirements and existing insurance systems to determine suitable software solutions.
•	Design, develop and configure software applications and system components across various application modules.
•	Write, modify and maintain program code in accordance with approved technical specifications, coding standards and project requirements.
•	Create and maintain integrations between various applications, internal systems, databases, multiple enterprise platforms and third-party services.
•	Interpret functional requirements, user stories, process models and technical designs to support accurate software development.
•	Provide estimation for cost and resources required for the development of the software solutions.
•	Test, debug and correct software errors across development, system testing, user acceptance and production environments.
•	Develop and execute unit, integration, regression and automated tests to ensure software quality, reliability and performance.
•	Participate in code reviews, technical quality assurance activities and system health checks to ensure compliance with development standards.
•	Investigate production incidents and provide second- and third-level technical support for business-critical insurance applications.
•	Prepare and maintain technical documentation covering application designs, configurations, integrations, program logic, testing outcomes and deployment procedures.
•	Mentor team members/other engineers/developers and promote best engineering practices

Qualifications, Experience and Technical Skills:
•	Relevant Degree in Technology or related fields
•	A minimum of 10-15 years of work experience in a similar job role
•	Extensive experience in Java Development, Kubernetes, Angular or React
•	Guidewire experience is highly desirable 
•	Strong proficiency in Java, C# and ECMAScript.
•	Experience with full-stack application development.
•	Knowledge of APIs and system integrations.
•	Substantial understanding of Spring Boot, Kubernetes, and Agentic AI (Anthropic/Claude preferred)
•	Strong communication, negotiations and leadership skills
•	Exceptional organisational and time-management skills
•	Experience with cloud-based development environments.
•	Strong debugging and problem-solving skills.


 Australian citizens and permanent residents are preferred.
If this sounds like the role for you, please apply via the facilities provided on this website. Due to a high volume of applications, please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted.

AI Talent, a pioneer in AI-powered solutions, is looking for a meticulous and experienced Software Tester to join our team. Weldworks is hiring a Full-time Construction Project Manager role in West Ryde, NSW. Apply now to be part of our team.

Requirements for this role:

Flexible hours available
2–3 years of relevant work experience required for this role
WELDWORKS PTY LTD is looking for an experienced Construction Project Manager for our client’s construction projects, including residential homes, commercial buildings, civil works and public spaces in Sydney.
On a full-time basis, you will be responsible for planning, organising, directing, controlling and coordinating construction projects, as well as managing the physical, financial and human resources involved in the construction process.

Title: Construction Project Manager, Full-time position
Salary: A$ 90,000.00 to 98,000.00 plus super
Work Location: In person
We are looking for applicants who demonstrate the following:

Requirements
•	Bachelor’s degree or higher in Construction Project Management, Construction Management, Building Technology, Building Science, Civil Engineering or another highly relevant field. 
•	At least 2–3 years of relevant experience managing residential, commercial, industrial or civil construction projects. 
•	Demonstrated experience managing construction schedules, budgets, labour, materials, plant and equipment. 
•	Strong knowledge of construction methods, building legislation, Australian Standards, quality requirements and workplace health and safety procedures. 
•	Ability to read, assess and interpret architectural drawings, engineering plans, specifications and construction contracts. 
•	Experience coordinating architects, engineers, consultants, subcontractors, suppliers, tradespeople and relevant authorities. 
•	Strong understanding of tendering, procurement, contract administration and project cost control. 
•	Ability to identify project risks, delays and budget variations and implement appropriate corrective actions. 
•	Strong leadership, communication, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills. 
•	Excellent organisational, reporting and problem-solving abilities. 
•	Current Australian driver licence preferred. 
•	Relevant registration, licence or site accreditation may be required depending on the project and scope of work. 

Construction Project Manager Responsibilities
•	Plan, organise, direct, control and coordinate construction projects from commencement through to completion. 
•	Establish project plans, construction schedules, milestones, budgets and resource requirements. 
•	Interpret architectural drawings, engineering plans, technical specifications and contractual requirements. 
•	Determine appropriate construction methods, sequencing, labour requirements, materials, plant and equipment. 
•	Coordinate the procurement and delivery of construction materials, equipment and services. 
•	Consult with architects, engineers, building professionals, consultants, tradespeople and technical workers. 
•	Negotiate and communicate with building owners, property developers, clients, suppliers and subcontractors. 
•	Prepare, review and contribute to tenders, quotations, contract bids and project proposals. 
•	Implement coordinated work programs across construction sites. 
•	Monitor project progress, expenditure, quality, safety, risk and compliance against approved plans and budgets. 
•	Ensure construction activities comply with relevant building legislation, Australian Standards, contractual requirements and workplace health and safety procedures. 
•	Manage and monitor the performance, quality and progress of contractors and subcontractors. 
•	Arrange the submission of plans, permits and supporting documents to relevant authorities. 
•	Coordinate required inspections, approvals and project handover activities. 
•	Prepare progress reports, budget updates, risk assessments and project documentation. 
•	Identify potential delays, cost overruns, quality issues and construction risks and implement appropriate corrective actions. 
•	Lead and supervise site managers, project engineers, supervisors, forepersons, subcontractors and tradespeople as required. 
•	Maintain effective communication with clients and key stakeholders throughout the construction process. 
•	Ensure projects are completed safely, on time, within budget and in accordance with the required quality standards. 

These responsibilities reflect the official ANZSCO functions for Construction Project Managers, including management of construction 
schedules, procurement, contractors, budgets, compliance, inspections and project resources. 
If you would like to discuss the role further, please click APPLY and send through an up-to-date CV. We can schedule a time to discuss the position available and determine whether the role is suitable for your qualifications and experience.
Work Location: In person
